body:
After a lot and trial and error on #295 the following was learned:

 * GitHub Actions no longer accept files to be created on /tmp. Instead `$RUNNER_TEMP` should be used. See [this article](https://nesin.io/blog/temp-directory-path-github-actions). Changes were made accordingly.
 * Further, pip no longer can be used on global environment, which is required to install perceval. A venv must be created. Therefore, the github actions workflows were updated to reflect that. Also, Venv was placed above the directory all actions execute (which is `$RUNNER_TEMP`/kaiaulu/kaiaulu). Failing that, the Check will find the .venv folder within Kaiaulu, failing the pass.
 * Perceval restriction to use version 0.12.4 has been lifted, as I can now test on my local machine the more recent version. The workflows were updated to reflect the version that is being tested locally by me (as I do not have the bandwidth to test every possible version). 
 * OS X version on GitHub Actions was also updated.
 * Various actions versions were updated since they had since been deprecated. 

Perhaps the most substantial change was the addition to the `tmp` variable to `tools.yml`. This is because the way GitHub Actions determine the tmp folder is now different than a local machine (which is just `/tmp`). As such, Kaiaulu needs to know where to place the intermediate files when creating unit tests. In the long run, parameterizing this is beneficial because it accommodates Windows users. 

Something worth noting is the R/examples.R needs some work to diagnose why it keeps throwing warnings. I waste a substantial amount of time looking to solve them on Github Actions just to realize they were already there all along and were not the cause of the errors.

As I had to prototype this on an actual PR to see it is in working order, the changes will be bundled with #295 . This is not ideal, but the changes are isolated to tests, and .workflow folder, so it should be easy to tell them apart even in one commit.

Note to self: Write a wrapper for github_api_project_pull_request_refresh() that calls:

```r
issue_or_pr <- "is:pull-request"
gh_response <- github_api_project_issue_refresh(owner, repo, token, save_path_pull_request, issue_or_pr)
```

Since it fundamentally achieves the same thing. It is currently being used in the notebook as a workaround since the original function that is implemented was found at the last moment to lack a temporal parameter. This workaround functions just fine in being equivalent. 

Also decide on all these new functions being added to the API:

create_file_directory, create_file_path, get_github_pr_comments_path, get_github_pr_commits_path, get_github_pr_files_path, get_github_pr_merge_path, get_github_pr_reviewers_path, github_api_issue_pr_comments, github_api_pr_commits, github_api_pr_files, github_api_pr_merge, github_api_pr_reviewers, github_api_pr_reviews_refresh, github_api_project_pr_comments, github_api_project_pr_comments_refresh, github_api_project_pull_request_refresh, github_api_pull_pr_comments, github_api_pull_request, github_parse_project_pr_comments, github_parse_project_pr_commits, github_parse_project_pr_files, github_parse_project_pr_merge, github_parse_project_pr_reviewers, github_parse_project_pr_reviews, github_parse_pull_request

performed_via_github_app.description:
Codecov provides highly integrated tools to group, merge, archive and compare coverage reports. Whether your team is comparing changes in a pull request or reviewing a single commit, Codecov will improve the code review workflow and quality.

## Code coverage done right.®

1. Upload coverage reports from your CI builds.
2. Codecov merges all builds and languages into one beautiful coherent report.
3. Get commit statuses, pull request comments and coverage overlay via our browser extension.

When Codecov merges your uploads it keeps track of the CI provider (inc. build details) and user specified context, e.g. `#unittest` ~ `#smoketest` or `#oldcode` ~ `#newcode`. You can track the `#unittest` coverage independently of other groups. [Learn more here](
http://docs.codecov.io/docs/flags)

Through **Codecov's Browser Extension** reports overlay directly in GitHub UI to assist in code review in [Chrome](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/codecov/gedikamndpbemklijjkncpnolildpbgo) or Firefox (https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/codecov/)

*Highly detailed* **pull request comments** and *customizable* **commit statuses** will improve your team's workflow and code coverage incrementally.

**File backed configuration** all through the `codecov.yml`. 

## FAQ
- Do you **merge multiple uploads** to the same commit? **Yes**
- Do you **support multiple languages** in the same project? **Yes**
- Can you **group coverage reports** by project and/or test type? **Yes**
- How does **pricing** work? Only paid users can view reports and post statuses/comments.
